A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiCo research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–G are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, architecture and component ablations, scaling measurements and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds MS-COCO text-to-image experiments, ImageNet 1024×1024 evaluation, and FlowDCN and modern-DiT comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds two text-conditioning mechanisms after each Conv Module: cross-attention and dynamic 9×9 depthwise kernels derived from CLIP embeddings. Algorithm 1 implements the latter. These introduce new inputs and block computations beyond v1's class-conditioned model; the original backbone and CCA remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on MS-COCO for text-to-image generation and an ImageNet 1024×1024 generation scenario. v1 evaluates DiCo only on class-conditional ImageNet at 256×256 and 512×512; its existing PixArt/FLUX attention visualizations do not constitute DiCo text-to-image evaluation.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets are retained. New Table 3 introduces text-to-image comparisons including AttnGAN, DM-GAN, U-Net, U-ViT-S/2, MMDiT and MMDiT+REPA. Appendix Tables 12–13 add comparisons involving FlowDCN-S/2, SiT-S/2, REPA and LightningDiT.

E3.justification: New protocols include matched 33M models trained from scratch for 400K iterations at 1024×1024 without CFG, a 400K-iteration comparison retaining FlowDCN's isotropic architecture and training setup, and an 800-epoch modern-DiT comparison with a 679M proposed model. Original ImageNet training settings remain unchanged. Table 1 also relabels throughput from it/s to image/s without explaining a measurement change.

E4.justification: v2 compares cross-attention with text-conditioned depthwise convolution and tests replacing MultiScale DCN with the Conv Module while retaining FlowDCN's architecture and training setup. These add focused component analyses. Existing architecture, activation, kernel-size, CCA and attention ablations, together with scaling analyses, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Original numerical results are retained. New results include MS-COCO FIDs 4.87/4.93 for the two DiCo variants, versus 4.14 for MMDiT+REPA; 1024×1024 FID 102.60 versus DiT's 113.06; and FlowDCN-setting FID 52.1 versus 54.6. Table 13 reports FID 1.33 versus LightningDiT's 1.35 under a new 800-epoch setup, not a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The diffusion formulation, losses, classifier-free guidance expression and CCA equation are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs; the new conditioning algorithm is a procedural addition.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion now claim experimentally demonstrated text-to-image potential, previously future work. v2 removes the explicit claim of being the first fully convolutional backbone to achieve SOTA diffusion performance and narrows broad superiority language to recent models and specified comparisons. Original ImageNet numerical claims remain in the paper.

C2.justification: Appendix F removes the limitation that text-to-image generation was unexplored while retaining the model-scale limitation. New discussion interprets MS-COCO results as supporting larger-scale text-to-image applicability. Appendix D's explicit caveat about not surpassing every generative model is removed; the original locality and channel-redundancy explanations remain.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds tensor shapes, padding, reshaping and grouped-convolution implementation details; the text identifies CLIP's 77-token input and module placement. v2 also explicitly states that existing ablations omit CFG. Original configuration, hardware and training-time tables and the repository pointer remain unchanged, while pointers to uncompressed supplementary samples are removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted citations and discussion for FlowDCN, LightningDiT and text-to-image methods, and withdraws the explicit first-fully-convolutional-SOTA priority claim. The existing related-work organization and central positioning of convolution as an efficient alternative to Transformers remain largely intact.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized abstract, contribution and conclusion revisions, new method and experimental paragraphs, acknowledgements and publication-header updates. Most explanatory prose and the main section and Appendix A–G organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds four compact comparison tables and Algorithm 1, introduces a Token Mixing Type column in Tables 1–2, and adjusts captions and placement. Existing diagrams, plots and sample-gallery images are retained; gallery running headers are removed. These are localized additions and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The controlled FlowDCN substitution and modern-DiT comparisons substantially strengthen evidence that the convolutional components remain competitive beyond the original setup. The implemented text-conditioning extension and MS-COCO evaluation establish applicability that v1 left untested, while 1024×1024 experiments strengthen efficiency-scaling evidence. More restrained novelty claims improve calibration. New protocols remain tersely documented and the text-to-image speed claim lacks timing figures, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation.
